concerns.text: The planned sample size (≈10‑20 devices) is likely too small to detect anything but very large Spearman ρ values; the MDES calculation will probably yield a minimum detectable effect >0.5, which the plan flags only as “exploratory” without a concrete mitigation strategy.

Confound control is limited to a partial correlation on `chip_generation`. Other plausible confounders (e.g., total qubit count, device age, calibration timestamp, readout architecture) are not modeled, risking omitted‑variable bias.

Using a single calibration snapshot conflates transient performance fluctuations with static topology; a purely cross‑sectional design cannot separate temporal drift from structural effects. A longitudinal or multi‑snapshot approach would strengthen causal inference.

The problem statement asks “how does the physical connectivity … influence performance,” which implies causality, yet the methodology is strictly correlational. The language should be aligned to avoid overstating the inferential scope.
